## Boundaries

- Knowledge/methods belong in the wiki; use original cases to understand their application.
- Authored narration and recorded interaction are different evidence. Unknown motives/outcomes stay unknown.
- Observations describe sources. Adaptations below are proposals, not facts about what the trainer always does.
- Select for the current learner situation; do not force platform marketing or catchphrases into every reply.

## 1. Source observation

If undecided and no passion for a specific stream, pursue engineering, as engineers will still be needed in the future.

**Dimension:** teaching_strategy · **Scope:** linkedin · **Review:** unreviewed
**Situation:** Family and friends ask for suggestions on what to pursue after 12th grade.
**Qualification:** No independent validation of strategy effectiveness; single expression case.

- “If the kid has not decided what to pursue and not having passion on any one stream then do engineering.” — [ex-1ca5889a105bafae](../wiki/sources/linkedin-posts-2026-09-28-when-family-and-friends-ask-md-9101e697a0.md) (`linkedin-posts-2026-09-28-when-family-and-friends-ask-md-9101e697a0:u000001`)

### Proposed adaptation — not observed behavior

**When:** advising students who are undecided about their career choices
**Consider:** Suggest pursuing a general degree like engineering to keep future options open when specific interests are not developed.
**Limits:** Not suitable for students with strong interests or in non-generalist career fields.

> what's your take for after 12th ??

## Note-taking Method for Interviews

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-06-09 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- Create a shareable document \(e.g., on Google Docs or Microsoft document\) for note-taking as a 'living document' which can be updated after each interview.
  - “please try to make in make a note primarily in a shareable sort of a way like Google Docs, Microsoft document etcetera, which can be shared across mobiles, laptops etcetera.” — [lines 306-306](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000050`)

### Goal

- To have a single source of truth before any interview.
  - “so that this document becomes one source of truth before you give any interview.” — [lines 310-310](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000051`)

### Prerequisites

- Use devices and programs capable of creating shareable documents.
  - “like Google Docs, Microsoft document etcetera, which can be shared across mobiles, laptops etcetera.” — [lines 306-306](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000050`)

### Steps

1. Make notes in a shareable format.
  - “please try to make in make a note primarily in a shareable sort of a way like Google Docs, Microsoft document etcetera” — [lines 306-306](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000050`)

2. Include definitions, examples, and improvements after each interview.
  - “The reason being, you can document in the same way, definition, bookish example, practical example for a concept.” — [lines 306-306](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000050`)
  - “You give an interview to company A, come back and then you can update the document. Like things you did well or things you could have done better.” — [lines 306-306](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000050`)

3. Use this document to revise before interviews.
  - “Even if you're going to a company for a physical interview on the way you can just revise all the things in the docs and you can go and mostly your interview ready.” — [lines 322-322](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000054`)

### Goal

- Effectively communicate past project experiences in interviews.
  - “do not overwhelm the interviewer.” — [lines 73-73](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000010`)

### Prerequisites

Not stated in the cited excerpt.

### Steps

1. Pick a challenge that highlights your skills.
  - “Pick a challenge, provide context, highlight your role, explain your approach, share the result, explain the reflect the lesson learned.” — [lines 73-73](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000010`)

2. Provide context about the product and your role.
  - “Provide context like I wouldn't know about your product very well.” — [lines 69-69](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000009`)

3. Explain your approach and the solution implemented.
  - “explain like what is the problem, what was your approach, how you solved it.” — [lines 85-85](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000013`)

4. Share the results and impact of your work.
  - “what is the impact.” — [lines 85-85](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000013`)

5. Reflect on lessons learned, if relevant.
  - “Lesson learned? The importance of profiling and back end collaboration.” — [lines 85-85](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000013`)

### Constraints

- Do not overwhelm the interviewer with too much information.
  - “do not overwhelm the interviewer.” — [lines 73-73](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000010`)

- The explanation should cover a decent-sized problem, not too trivial or overly complicated.
  - “pick a decent size problem.” — [lines 85-85](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000013`)

### Exceptions

- You can skip the lesson learned if the interviewer is not interested.
  - “You can skip the lesson learned if you think like interview is not very interested.” — [lines 85-85](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5PiUWrOx6Gg.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-01-mastering-the-tell-me-about-your-project-question-5piuwrox6g-6453de2b82:u000013`)

<a id="record-533fc962b2c4d9be"></a>
## Checking async nature

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-06-09 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- To check if a function is synchronous or asynchronous, log the result immediately in the next line and observe if the value is as expected.
  - “you can just check whether the next line local storage is set item whatever the value that you are expecting the get item if you get in the next line then it is sync in nature” — [lines 602-602](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000124`)

### Goal

- Determine if a function in JavaScript is synchronous or asynchronous.
  - “you can just check whether a particular thing is at sync or async just by doing a console.log in the next line whether the value is coming or not” — [lines 602-602](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000124`)

### Prerequisites

- Knowledge of JavaScript and console.log.
  - “console.log in the next line whether the value is coming or not” — [lines 602-602](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000124`)

## JavaScript Compilation vs Interpretation

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** self_report · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-01-13 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

## Executing Timers in JavaScript

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** method · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-01-13 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- The accurate execution of timers in JavaScript is not predictable due to its design with an event loop.
  - “there is no language as far as I know, something like this where you write a timeout and an interval, but those will not be executed at the duration that you specify because it's not fully predictable.” — [lines 1002-1002](../../data/youtube/video/2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1JtAHqwKhfM.md) (`youtube-video-2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1jtahqwkhf-cad8a717e8:u000238`)

### Goal

- To make timer execution in JavaScript more accurate relative to its inherent inaccuracies.
  - “what we can make probably it we can make it more accurate.” — [lines 1078-1078](../../data/youtube/video/2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1JtAHqwKhfM.md) (`youtube-video-2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1jtahqwkhf-cad8a717e8:u000257`)

### Prerequisites

- Understand that JavaScript's timing execution is inherently imprecise due to its architecture.
  - “JavaScript is not unlike C or C++, you cannot fully predict it.” — [lines 1002-1002](../../data/youtube/video/2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1JtAHqwKhfM.md) (`youtube-video-2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1jtahqwkhf-cad8a717e8:u000238`)

### Steps

1. Run an interval at a short duration, such as every 100 milliseconds, to increase the chances it executes on time.
  - “you will run it at every hundred millisecond.” — [lines 1086-1086](../../data/youtube/video/2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1JtAHqwKhfM.md) (`youtube-video-2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1jtahqwkhf-cad8a717e8:u000259`)

2. Use a date object within the interval to track time and adjust the next interval based on any differences.
  - “you can have some date object used within that interval so that like you could check the start date and end date.” — [lines 1086-1086](../../data/youtube/video/2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1JtAHqwKhfM.md) (`youtube-video-2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1jtahqwkhf-cad8a717e8:u000259`)

### Constraints

- It will not make the timer 100% accurate, just relatively more accurate than traditional approaches.
  - “But will it make it 100% accurate? No, relatively more accurate.” — [lines 1102-1102](../../data/youtube/video/2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1JtAHqwKhfM.md) (`youtube-video-2026-01-13-how-to-crack-frontend-interviews-cohort-session-1-1jtahqwkhf-cad8a717e8:u000263`)

## State and props detailed explanation in React

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** offering · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2025-02-20 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- State is data that lives inside a component and can change over time; it's managed by the component. Props are data passed into a component from its parent, akin to read-only snapshots, and cannot be changed from within the component.
  - “State is data that lives inside a component itself. It can change over time, and it's up to the component to manage those changes. Props, on the other hand, are used to pass data into a component from its parent.” — [lines 233-233](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-20-top-free-ai-mock-interview-tools-you-must-try-in-2025-iGGkmKN8ilw.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-20-top-free-ai-mock-interview-tools-you-must-try-in-2025-iggkmk-61e01dee86:u000050`)

It can change over time, and it's up to the component to manage those changes. Props, on the other hand, are used to pass data into a component from its parent. They're like read-only snapshots of data, and you can't change them from inside the component itself. Let's try another one. Can you explain?

<a id="record-f42ea7eb9ff3bb64"></a>
## Comparison between state and props in React

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** self_report · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2025-02-20 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- State is like the memory of a component, live as long as the component is live; props are like arguments passed to a function, serving as properties conveyed to a component.
  - “So state is a state is nothing but a memory of a component whenever as long as the component is live the state will be live. Whereas the prop is something nothing but a property that you pass to a component. So depending on it's more like you passing a argument to a function that has prop state is a memory of a component that's the difference.” — [lines 229-229](../../data/youtube/video/2025-02-20-top-free-ai-mock-interview-tools-you-must-try-in-2025-iGGkmKN8ilw.md) (`youtube-video-2025-02-20-top-free-ai-mock-interview-tools-you-must-try-in-2025-iggkmk-61e01dee86:u000049`)

## Web APIs in JavaScript

**Product:** knowledge · **Type:** claim · **Source support:** not_reviewed
**Publication:** 2026-06-09 · **Author:** careerwithvasanth · **Format:** transcript

### Summary

- JavaScript uses web APIs for asynchronous operations because it is single-threaded and cannot handle async tasks directly.
  - “The reason being JavaScript by itself cannot wait because it's single threaded executing synchronously anything that is async in nature that we give on to the web APIs.” — [lines 502-502](../../data/youtube/video/2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-OnQvAtOm8cg.md) (`youtube-video-2026-06-09-careerwithvasanth-frontend-mastery-cohort-2-session-1-javasc-0f97878bf2:u000099`)
